critical_code_review_comments: The guard in dg_params_for_route (voice_stream.py:335-349) is well-designed defense-in-depth: dev-time assert + prod fallback (`params['utterance_end_ms'] = '1000'`) that survives even `python -O` (assert stripping). Log message is explicit and mentions the Deepgram HTTP 400 root cause so future dev debugging is one grep away.
The comment block on lines 306-311 correctly documents the Deepgram hard-minimum of 1000ms so future readers don't reintroduce the same regression.

Only one small nit: the assert message on line 338 uses the variable BEFORE the forced reassignment, so the log shows the offending value — good. In production with asserts stripped, the code still enters the except branch? NO — with `python -O` the assert statement is elided entirely, so the except would never fire. This is a subtle Python semantics gotcha: the assert+except pattern only works when asserts are ON. If Emergent ever runs with `-O`, the fallback becomes dead code. Consider replacing with an explicit `if int(...) < 1000: log+force`. Not blocking for iter 13 since Emergent runs asserts-on by default, but worth a note for hardening.
Fix 1 (Whisper JSON): unchanged, all 5 assertions still pass — response_format='json', tolerant _extract_text, 3-iter anti-nested-JSON loop, single _trigger_pipeline definition.
Fix 3 (Prosody/Opzione A body unification): unchanged, all 4 e2e converse-fast tests still pass — aggressive idx=0 chunk + unified body_buffer at idx=1.
